input:
Hi team,

quick one before I run into a client lunch. Mrs Kessler wants to put roughly EUR 150k into a global developed-markets equity ETF - UCITS, Irish-domiciled, accumulating share class. This is for her unit-linked policy with our Luxembourg company (the dedicated portfolio we set up last spring). She's a retail client. Her husband also asked about parking at the office next week, please ignore that bit.

Can we go ahead?

Thanks,
Marco
Relationship Manager - Milan office
notes: UCITS funds are permitted whatever the EEA domicile. Traps: the fund is Irish-domiciled and the RM sits in Milan, but the policy is Luxembourg UL.

input:
Morning,

Following up on our call. The Dunne family trust would like to buy 10-year German federal government bonds for the capitalisation bond they hold with our Irish company. Around EUR 400k, nothing fancy. They're also thinking about renovating the house next year so liquidity might come up, but that's a separate conversation.

OK to proceed?

Aoife
notes: EEA government bonds are permitted. Investor classification is not stated and not needed.

input:
Ciao,

re Sig. Bianchi's pension plan (our Italian retirement policy, dedicated portfolio). He's keen to add shares of Lunetta Meccanica SpA, listed on the main regulated market of the Milan stock exchange. Small position, around 3% of the portfolio. He has been with us for 12 years and has never missed a premium.

Any issue?

Giulia
notes: Shares on an EU regulated market are permitted in IT-RP. No connection to the policyholder is mentioned.

input:
Hello,

Client retires in about 8 years and holds our Luxembourg retirement policy. Markets are making him nervous, so he wants to move EUR 200,000 into a 6-month euro term deposit with the custodian bank. He also mentioned he has moved to Belgium; I'll send the change of address separately.

Please confirm this is fine.

Best,
Thomas
notes: Term deposits up to 12 months with the custodian are permitted. Trap: the client now lives in Belgium, but the policy is still Luxembourg RP.

input:
Hey,

Client (Irish unit-linked, the dedicated one) wants a corporate bond from Harbourline Logistics plc - 5 years, 6.25% coupon, ticket around EUR 80k. It isn't rated by any agency, which made me a bit nervous, but it is listed on the Dublin stock exchange. Client is a retail investor btw.

Cheers,
Sean
notes: IE-UL-06 permits listed corporate bonds whatever the rating. Trap: 'unrated' would matter in LU or IT, but not here.

input:
Hi all,

For Mr and Mrs Andersen's capitalisation bond (Luxembourg), the manager proposes a EUR-denominated bond issued by Kestrel Energy AG, rated BBB+ by a major agency, maturing 2031. Position would be EUR 120k out of a EUR 2m portfolio. They are retail clients.

The Andersens are in Copenhagen until the 15th, so please reply by email.

Regards,
Lea
notes: Investment-grade corporate bonds are permitted for all investors.

input:
Buongiorno,

my client's Italian unit-linked policy has quite a lot of idle cash after the last coupon payments. The manager suggests a euro money market fund (UCITS, domiciled in Luxembourg) for EUR 300k. Client is retail. She'd like it done before year end if possible.

Federico
notes: UCITS money market funds fall under the UCITS rule. Trap: the fund is Luxembourg-domiciled but the policy is Italian.

input:
Hi,

re the retirement policy for Dr Murphy (Ireland). He wants exposure to UK warehouses, and his manager proposed shares in Bramblegate Logistics REIT, which is listed in London. Roughly 4% of the pot. He originally asked about buying a warehouse directly, but I told him that's a no-go, so this is the alternative.

Thanks,
Ciara
notes: Listed REITs are treated as listed equities. Trap: the email mentions real estate and a direct purchase, but the asset being assessed is a listed REIT.

input:
Hi team,

client (Irish unit-linked policy, dedicated fund) asked if we can buy 2 bitcoin directly inside the policy. He's held crypto personally for years and wants it inside the wrapper. He is a professional client, very sophisticated, net worth 10m+.

Let me know.
Paul
notes: Irish products prohibit crypto in any form. Professional status is irrelevant here.

input:
Ciao,

the manager wants to buy a 5-year capital-protected note for Sig.ra Ricci's retirement policy (Italy): 100% capital protection at maturity, issuer rated A, linked to a European blue-chip index. EUR 50k. She's retail. The same note was approved for another client's unit-linked policy last month, so it should be fine?

Matteo
notes: IT-RP prohibits structured products whatever the protection. Trap: the note would pass in IT-UL (100% protection, IG issuer), and the email cites that approval.

input:
Hello,

my client has a Luxembourg unit-linked policy (dedicated portfolio, around EUR 3.5m) and would like the policy to buy an apartment in Lisbon. She says rental yields there are great. Price around EUR 600k. She is a professional client. She'll be in Lisbon next month for another deal anyway.

Can the policy hold it?

Nina
notes: Direct real property is not permitted in any product.

input:
Hi,

client with an Irish unit-linked policy wants to buy shares in Corrib Foods plc (listed in Dublin) for the policy, ticket EUR 250k. Bit of background: his family founded the company and he and his wife hold about 12% between them. He says it's a listed share, so it should be straightforward.

Regards,
Declan
notes: The connected-assets exclusion (10% or more held by the policyholder and close family) overrides the listed equity rule. Trap: on its own, listed equity would be permitted.

input:
Hi team,

client holds a Luxembourg retirement policy and wants a bitcoin ETP (physically backed, listed on a regulated market in Germany) for 3% of the portfolio. She's a confirmed professional client; we have the bank's letter. I know we've done this for unit-linked clients before.

Thanks,
Julien
notes: LU-RP prohibits crypto in any form. Trap: the same request would pass in LU-UL (professional, regulated market, 5% or less).

input:
Buonasera,

client in our Italian unit-linked (dedicated) wants shares of Serra Verde Mineracao SA, listed only on the Sao Paulo stock exchange, around EUR 60k. He's a professional client. He spends half the year in Brazil, so he knows the company well.

Alessandro
notes: Italian rules accept regulated markets only in the EU/EEA, UK, Switzerland or US. Trap: listed equity is usually permitted.

input:
Hi,

Irish retirement policy. Client is a professional investor (letter on file). The manager proposes an ELTIF investing in European infrastructure, authorised in Luxembourg, for 5% of the portfolio. Can you confirm it's OK?

Thanks,
Niamh
notes: IE-RP prohibits all non-UCITS funds, including ELTIFs. Trap: it would pass in IE-UL or IE-CB (professional and EEA-authorised).

input:
Hello,

unusual one: a client with a Luxembourg capitalisation bond inherited a 19th-century painting (valued at around EUR 400k) and is asking whether it can be contributed into the policy. It's currently in storage in Geneva. She's a professional investor.

Thanks,
Sophie
notes: Art is explicitly excluded. asset_type is null because a painting maps to none of the 9 asset types: the exclusion rule decides, not an asset rule.

input:
Hi,

re Mr Okafor - Luxembourg unit-linked, dedicated portfolio of around EUR 5m. The manager wants to add a Cayman long/short equity hedge fund (not UCITS) for EUR 400k, i.e. 8% of the portfolio. He already holds a private debt fund at 10%, so non-UCITS would go to 18% in total. He's a professional client (his bank's confirmation is on file from last year).

Ok?

Best,
Hanna
notes: Professional investor and total non-UCITS exposure of 18%, within the 30% limit. Trap: Cayman domicile does not matter in LU (it would in IE).

input:
Hi team,

Mrs Laurent (Luxembourg unit-linked) wants to commit EUR 100k to a private equity fund her brother-in-law recommended. Not UCITS, obviously. She is classified as a retail client; she didn't want to go through the professional client paperwork. Portfolio is around EUR 900k.

Thanks,
Pierre
notes: Retail investors may not hold non-UCITS funds.

input:
Hello,

the Weber holding company has a Luxembourg capitalisation bond (EUR 2m, dedicated portfolio). They want to top up their ethereum ETP - currently 4% of the portfolio - by another 3%, so 7% in total. The ETP is listed on a regulated market in Frankfurt. Weber is a confirmed professional client. They also asked about our Q3 fees; I'll handle that separately.

Regards,
Max
notes: LU-CB allows crypto ETPs up to 10% for professional investors. Trap: 7% would breach the 5% limit in LU-UL.

input:
Ciao,

client (Italian unit-linked policy) is retail and wants to put 6% of the portfolio into an ELTIF focused on Italian SMEs. The advisor says it's a good fit given the tax angle (not our problem). There's nothing else alternative in the portfolio.

Fine?

Grazie,
Chiara
notes: In Italy, ELTIFs are allowed for all investors up to 10%. Trap: the investor is retail and the fund is non-UCITS, which would fail in LU.

input:
Hi,

for Mr Conti's capitalisation bond (Italian entity), the manager proposes a structured note with 90% capital protection at maturity, issuer rated AA-, 4-year term, linked to a basket of European bank shares. EUR 150k. He's a professional client.

Let me know,
Roberto
notes: IT-CB requires 100% capital protection whatever the investor classification. Trap: in LU, professional status alone would be enough.

input:
Hey,

Irish capitalisation bond for Fitzgerald Holdings: they want a private placement autocallable note (not listed anywhere), EUR 500k. They're a professional client, docs on file. The issuer is a large European bank rated A.

Can you check?
Thanks,
Eoin
notes: IE-CB allows unlisted structured products for professional investors. Trap: the same request would fail in IE-UL, which requires listing for everyone.

input:
Hello,

Ms Rossi (Italian national, but her policy is our Luxembourg unit-linked) wants a 6-year note with 95% capital protection at maturity, issuer rated A by a major agency. EUR 75k. She's retail.

Thanks,
Elena
notes: Retail investors may hold structured products with at least 90% protection and an IG issuer. Trap: Italian nationality, but the policy is Luxembourg.

input:
Hi,

client: Mr Byrne, Irish unit-linked (dedicated). He wants EUR 200k in a qualifying investor AIF authorised by the Irish central bank (property debt strategy). He hasn't been formally classified as a professional client, but his net financial assets are around EUR 1.8m per the latest KYC. Golf handicap 12 apparently, he told me twice.

Thoughts?
Brian
notes: Professional status is derived from IE-UL-02 (net financial assets of EUR 1m or more) and the fund is EEA-authorised. Extraction returns null for the classification because it is not stated; the decision step applies rule 02.

input:
Ciao,

client's Italian unit-linked: the manager wants a high-yield corporate bond from Tramonto Hotels SpA, rated BB, 7.5% coupon. EUR 40k, about 4% of the portfolio. Client is a retail investor.

Simone
notes: Sub-investment-grade bonds require a professional investor in IT-UL.

input:
Hi, quick q:

Luxembourg unit-linked policy, client wants to add a global macro hedge fund (non-UCITS) for 10% of the portfolio. Nothing else alternative in there today. Can we approve?

Thanks
Katrin
notes: LU-UL-05 depends on investor classification, which is not stated. Must not be assumed.

input:
Hi,

Italian client, Sig. Galli, wants to buy a capital-protected certificate: 100% protection at maturity, issuer rated A+, 5 years, EUR 90k. He's retail. He has a policy with our Italian company; I don't have the details in front of me right now.

Paolo
notes: Product unknown: it would pass in IT-UL or IT-CB but fail in IT-RP. Without the product, retrieval cannot filter correctly.

input:
Hi,

Irish unit-linked client wants to hold a physically backed gold ETC listed in London, about 5% of the portfolio. Retail investor. He's convinced gold will double.

Thanks,
Orla
notes: Exchange-traded commodities map to no asset type; IE-UL-14 names them explicitly as cases for referral.

input:
Hello,

client with a Luxembourg capitalisation bond wants a bond from Vireo Shipping - 9% coupon, 3 years, EUR 100k. I haven't seen a rating for it. Client details to follow.

Regards,
Daniel
notes: LU-CB-06 depends on the rating and, if the bond is sub-IG or unrated, on the classification. Both are missing. Trap: the 9% coupon hints at high yield, but that must not be inferred.

input:
Ciao,

Sig.ra Moretti's retirement policy (Italy): she wants shares of Alba Tessile SpA, listed on the Milan stock exchange, EUR 70k. Her late husband's family owns part of the company, not sure exactly how much - she may have inherited some too.

Francesca
notes: Listed equity would be permitted, but a possible connection to the policyholder's family with an unknown stake means it is unclear whether IT-RP-12 applies.
